principle: An agent is judged on whether its output is acted on, never on how much it produces. An agent that only produces volume gets switched off.
agents: falsifier: clean run — nothing failed, which is the point of it
review-agents: has never actually run (no key) — costing nothing, proving nothing, and honest about both
problems: creator: OVER-BUDGET — 15 findings against a ceiling of 10. An unreadable list is an unread list.

workforce.why: Nothing reads the Discord. Members ask questions our instruments cannot answer and we never see the pattern. The strongest roadmap input we have is unread. (needs the bot)
Nothing measures which of our own content lands. We generate six angles a day and learn nothing from which ones people use. (needs analytics or creator feedback)
Nothing tracks what other tools ship. We would learn a competitor solved something we are still guessing at only by accident. (web research, no new dependency)
Nothing spot-checks our published prices against the live marketplace by eye. Every guard we have compares us to ourselves. (needs a browser — CC's lane)

workforce.what: the shape this workforce is aiming at
workforce.why: Right now every agent watches US. A workforce that builds the best community, app, tools and database in this hobby needs agents that watch the MARKET (what changed that we did not notice), the COMMUNITY (what people are asking), and the FIELD (what everyone else shipped). Two of those three need the bot; one needs only research. That is the order to hire in.

chat.what: Artist angles all carry their sources.
chat.do: Extend the same to every angle in the post bank, and put the source in the script so it can be said aloud.

chat.what: "TCG prices" — we can answer this today with the index, per-product prices, and the deal zone.
chat.do: Make sure an angle exists for it in the daily bank. A lane we can win and do not generate content for is a wasted advantage.

chat.what: "track the market" — we can answer this today with the sealed index, its value-weighted twin, breadth, and per-class indexes.
chat.do: Make sure an angle exists for it in the daily bank. A lane we can win and do not generate content for is a wasted advantage.

chat.what: "hidden gems" — partly served by the floor-to-median lens and the artist underrated detector.
chat.do: Nothing surfaces hidden gems for SEALED — the artist version only covers singles. A sealed product priced far below its cohort is the same idea and we do not compute it.

chat.what: The Today screen carries 17 sections: The Daily Three, 🗳 Rip or Hold?, Biggest movers, Set the app up for you, Movers, Release radar…
chat.do: Rank them by how often somebody would act on each, and move the bottom third behind a tap. Nothing is deleted — it stops competing.

chat.what: 5 things visibly change day to day: the Daily Three, a fact, shelf moves, yesterday's picks revisited, Rip or Hold.
chat.do: Good coverage — the gap is that a returning reader cannot TELL at a glance what is new since yesterday.

chat.what: A number appears above the fold on Today.
chat.do: Holds — check on a 390px screen that it is still above the fold with the banner and nav present.

chat.what: Nothing is gated — every instrument is readable immediately.
chat.do: Holds. Keep it that way as the Discord unlock arrives — unlock depth, never truth.

chat.what: The index has no matched sample today, so it cannot move.
chat.do: Expected on a fresh series — worth a line on the page saying so, rather than a number that looks stuck.

chat.what: The knowledge base holds 8 verified facts.
chat.do: This is the asset that compounds — instruments can be rebuilt in a weekend, a decade of sourced facts cannot. A steady few per week beats a burst.

chat.what: artist-instruments.json is written every run and read by nothing — not another script, not the feed.
chat.do: Either surface it (the app, the Pulse, a creator tool) or stop generating it. Work that runs daily and reaches nobody is the most expensive kind.

chat.what: era-history.json is written every run and read by nothing — not another script, not the feed.
chat.do: Either surface it (the app, the Pulse, a creator tool) or stop generating it. Work that runs daily and reaches nobody is the most expensive kind.

Corrupt it — empty object, missing top-level key, wrong types — and see which of its 4 readers notices. Then decide which of them SHOULD have.

cc.what: 10 distinct angles are ready each morning.
cc.do: Hold it. The risk now is the opposite — too many choices is its own paralysis, so lead with three and let the rest be a list.
The gap is that they are files in a repo. A creator needs them one tap from the angle they picked, not from a folder.

cc.what: 4 accent colours appear on the same surface.
cc.do: Reserve green for positive, red for negative, and let mode accent everything else. Gold stays a highlight, never a third voice.
Keep them for section headers and the ELI5 lollipop; drop them from anything carrying a number.

tyler.what: We hold both deal-zone room and per-pack economics for the same products.
tyler.do: A "rip or trade" tool could answer one question nobody else can: at today's prices, is this box worth more opened, sold sealed online, or traded at a table? Three numbers we already compute, one screen.

tyler.what: Print windows and shelf movement are computed separately and never combined.
tyler.do: A late-print set whose shelves are draining is a genuinely different situation from either signal alone. Crossing them is free and nobody publishes it.
